rendered: The separated cathode powder was calcined in air at 600 °C[1] for 2 h[2]. The stated purpose was to remove the surface coatings and the carbon black (CB) still present in the powder. The thermal analysis supports this choice: the TGA-DTG data show an organic coating layer losing about ~3.3 wt%[3] near ~350 °C[4] and CB losing about ~4.1 wt%[5] near ~550 °C[6], so both can be removed by calcining in air at the same temperature.
